reviews.title: packs a lot into a small space
reviews.comment: Of course that leads to some difficulties, such as reaching some of the connectors and screws. Also, the 2nd M2. nvme connector is on the back side, and is covered by a backplate/heatsink. Any sloppy moves while aligning that thing to be screwed back on can cause the protective / heat conductive film to be mangled. The final result is a very nice well-performing system. The onboard intel i225-V ethernet chip works fine @ 2.5GHz under Freebsd 13.1. Didn't try the WIFI. The provided wifi depends on the board revision. See the Gigabyte manual. One problem was the Amazon fulfillment: they first sent me a board that had been opened and fiddled with. So watch out. I returned it without trying it. The 2nd one was fine.
reviews.author: W.B.

reviews.title: Absolutely love this motherboard
reviews.comment: Needed an ITX motherboard for a 10" cube case I designed and chose this MB. Have tested it in Linux and Windows 10, both worked flawlessly. BIOS is decent and easy enough to navigate but I wish Gigabyte offered a couple other features but no big deal. Was surprised to see the actual ARGB lighting on the side of the MB which was fun. Overall, it works great.
reviews.author: Patrick Holmes

reviews.title: Terrible board for DDR4 enthusiasts.
reviews.comment: This is a review with the bios updated to F12 sept 2024, no other updates released as of March 2025. No EZ-debug lights(but rgb yes?), can''t run ram above 3400mhz when the same ram was running 4266 cl16 with the same cpu on the MSI equivalent B760i. I've tried 5 other kits and no luck, blue screens or black screen until cmos reset*. Bios is terrible, laggy, some sections are unresponsive until you click 15 times. There are settings that freeze the bios and the motherboard has no cmos reset button. You'll have to short the pins after opening your case and moving any cables/hardware that may be in the way. *Reseting the cmos will also delete any of your bios profiles so there's no point to even having the option to save one. MSI, EVGA, ASUS, does not delete you profiles and gets you back into the bios to change settings. That's the point of a cmos reset, not act like you reflashed the bios and start from square one. I'll leave it at that, but that's just the tip of the iceberg. Won't purchase Gigabyte ever again.
